title: Quiet Stepper Motor Controller
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

fixed_requirements.requirement: Stated requirements are authoritative; open choices must be made and documented as engineering decisions, not invented as hidden user requirements.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Treat stated requirements as authoritative; where the brief leaves choices open, make and document reasonable engineering decisions rather than inventing hidden user requirements.

open_decisions.decision: Which stepper driver device to use, and in which package.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires 'a modern quiet microstepping driver' and offers a Trinamic-class device only as an example; it names no part, vendor or package.

open_decisions.decision: Which MCU to use, in which package, and with what memory/peripheral set.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says only 'a small MCU' — no family, architecture, package or peripheral requirement is stated.

open_decisions.decision: How many current-sense resistors are used and on which phases, what sensing topology they sit in, and what resistance, tolerance, TCR, power rating and sense-connection scheme (Kelvin or otherwise) they use.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes that current-sense resistors are included (REQ-06), but fixes no value, tolerance, package, count per phase or sensing topology.

open_decisions.decision: How the driver is configured for microstep resolution, quiet-mode and current-regulation behaviour, decay and current scaling.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief asks for a 'quiet' microstepping driver and for configuration access, but states no microstep count, quiet-mode mechanism or current-regulation settings.

open_decisions.decision: How logic rails are generated from the 12–24 V input: regulator topology, rail voltage(s), and current budget.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes only the input supply range. It says nothing about logic voltage, regulator type or efficiency/thermal targets.

open_decisions.decision: Whether STEP/DIR is generated by the on-board MCU, driven from an external host connector, or both, and who owns motion profiling.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief lists STEP/DIR as an interface to include without saying which side of the board drives it or where motion planning lives.

open_decisions.decision: Whether both UART and SPI configuration paths are implemented, or one is selected, and how that path is exposed off-board.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief writes 'UART/SPI configuration access' without resolving whether the slash means both, either, or a build-time option.

open_decisions.decision: The host/control connector: family, pin count, pinout, and signal levels.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes a pin count only for the motor connector; the control-side connector is unspecified.

open_decisions.decision: The power-input connector: family, current rating, polarity keying and mounting style.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states the supply voltage range but nothing about how power enters the board.

open_decisions.decision: The 4-pin motor connector's family, pitch, per-contact current rating, orientation and retention.
open_decisions.why_open: Only the pin count is fixed by the brief; everything about the connector's physical and electrical spec is left open.

open_decisions.decision: The form of the fault/status signalling: visual indicator, digital output pin, driver register readback over the configuration bus, or a combination — and what conditions it reports.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires 'fault/status signals' without defining the medium, the fault set, or the latching/clearing behaviour.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, mounting-hole pattern, connector edge placement and any keepouts.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on mechanical constraints entirely.

open_decisions.decision: Stackup specifics: final layer count, layer assignment, copper weights and dielectric thicknesses.
open_decisions.why_open: Metadata records '4 preferred' as a preference rather than a fixed requirement, and neither brief nor metadata states copper weight or layer roles.

open_decisions.decision: The thermal strategy for driver dissipation: copper area, whether a thermal-via array is used and in what pattern, whether heat leaves through the pad into an internal or bottom plane, and the assumed ambient and airflow.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief directs attention to thermal-pad grounding but states no ambient, junction-temperature limit, airflow assumption or duty cycle, and prescribes no via or plane structure.

open_decisions.decision: Input protection strategy: reverse-polarity, overvoltage/transient handling on a 12–24 V rail, and ESD handling on exposed connectors.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief neither requires nor forbids protection; no environment, standard or immunity level is named.

open_decisions.decision: The grounding architecture — how power ground, sense return and MCU/logic ground relate (single pour, partitioned regions, stitching strategy) and where the single-point tie sits.
open_decisions.why_open: Mixed-signal grounding is listed as a stressor and thermal-pad grounding is called out, but no ground scheme is prescribed.

open_decisions.decision: Bulk capacitance value, technology, ripple-current rating and placement, and the ceramic decoupling set per rail.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires bulk/ceramic decoupling without specifying values, technologies or placement rules.

open_decisions.decision: Additional board features: enable/sleep/reset control, limit or endstop inputs, encoder or index inputs, test points, and programming/debug access for the MCU.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief lists no such features and does not exclude them; whether they are needed is a design judgement.

open_decisions.decision: Manufacturing and assembly constraints: fabricator and process class, single- vs double-sided assembly, and minimum trace/space and via geometry.
open_decisions.why_open: Neither the brief nor the metadata names a fabricator, process class or DFM ruleset.
